title: V-CoT: Vision Chain-of-Thought for Structured Reasoning Tasks

reviews.summary: Similar to chain-of-thought (CoT) approach which introduces explicit reasoning in large language models, multimodal chain-of-thought (m-CoT) has been proposed to boost up the performance of multimodal models. This work proposes a visual chain-of-thought (v-CoT) to boost up the performance on structured reasoning tasks, where part of the inputs are represented as images. v-CoT extracts task-specific propositions from the image, and reasons over the given task using the extracted propositions. The experimental results on 4 benchmarks demonstrate v-CoT outperforms prior approaches.
reviews.strengths:
1. The idea of v-CoT is simple and effective.
2. v-CoT outperforms prior state-of-the-art on all 4 benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness.
reviews.weaknesses:
1. The paper writing needs a major revision. 
2. More details are needed for annotation mentioned on L496-L497.
3. L495-L501 is hard to follow. Figure 5 seems not to match with its caption. The caption said “72%-85% cases for Chart QA and spider”, but the figure shows around 65%. Such unalignment can also be found on L500-501.
4. A further can be done to look into if there are any patterns for the failures mentioned on L525-L528. If this happens, it means with the oracle image perception, the language model cannot solve the tasks.


About writing
1. L48-L51 and L73-L77 both introduce v-CoT, which is redundant.
2. The spelling of v-CoT keeps varying, e.g., v-CoT (L77), v-COT (L285), v-CoT in verbatim (L316), VCoT (Figure 5 caption). This should be consistent.
3. Missing figure or table references on L320 and L513.
4. Resize Table 2 to make sure it is within one column.
5. Section 4.2 and 4.3 overlap a lot.
6. Table 4, “Model Props” has not been mentioned before. Is that “Image Props”?
